Parenting IBMA Consortium

HALFpipe Task-Based fMRI Analysis Manual

Image-Based Meta-Analysis of Parenting Constructs and Emotion-Processing Brain Activity

Written by Junxuan Zhao. Adapted for the Parenting IBMA project from the ENIGMA Task-Based fMRI Imaging Manual (Waller, Erk, Walter & Veer; based on the ENIGMA resting-state fMRI manual by Pozzi, Toenders, Veer, Waller, Haswell, Morey & Schmaal) and from the official HALFpipe documentation at fmri.science/halfpipe (About, Installation, and Manuals pages).

Questions and comments: junxuan@student.unimelb.edu.au

Before you begin: this manual assumes HALFpipe v1.3.2. Site-specific parenting-construct mappings, task contrasts, and analysis models referenced throughout are defined in your site's Site Confirmation Packet (Parenting Construct and fMRI Harmonization). Please keep that document open alongside this manual.

Summary

This manual takes each contributing site in the Parenting IBMA project through running HALFpipe on its local task-fMRI data, from data preparation through to the group-level summary statistics maps that will be pooled across sites for the image-based meta-analysis (IBMA).

No prior experience with HALFpipe is needed. This manual covers everything you will need, from data preparation through to the group-level summary statistics maps, in the following steps.

StepWhat you will do
1. Prepare for data analysisGather all data you will need, including anatomical scans, functional scans, event files, and parenting and demographic covariates.
2. Install a container platformInstall either Singularity/Apptainer or Docker to run HALFpipe.
3. Download HALFpipe & set up working directoryDownload HALFpipe v1.3.2, even if you already have a previous version installed.
4. Run preprocessing and feature extractionPerform preprocessing according to pre-specified parameters and extract first-level contrasts for each subject based on your Site Confirmation Packet.
5. Quality assessmentInspect HALFpipe's output and complete quality assessment in an interactive graphical interface, following the guidelines provided.
6. Group-level analysisRun group-level analysis for the harmonized parenting constructs defined in your Site Confirmation Packet.
7. Upload results for the IBMASubmit your site's outputs to the coordinating team. Deadline: 31 December 2026

Step 1. Prepare for Data Analysis

1.1 Hardware and Software Prerequisites

  • A computer with at least 8 GB of RAM.
  • At least ~0.6–1 GB of free disk space per subject for intermediate files, plus ~5.3 GB for the HALFpipe Singularity/Apptainer image (or ~23 GB if using Docker) and ~0.1 GB for the atlas/seed files.
  • Multiple CPU cores will speed up processing but are not required.
  • Running on a high-performance compute cluster (HPC) is recommended for larger sites and is faster and more resource-efficient. This manual gives instructions for both Local Machine and HPC Cluster workflows.
  • A FreeSurfer license file. This is free — request one via the FreeSurfer Registration form; the license is emailed to you within minutes.

1.2 Files Needed Per Subject

  1. Raw (non-skull-stripped) 3D T1-weighted anatomical image, .nii or .nii.gz. De-faced images work out of the box; if only skull-stripped anatomicals are available, see the note in Section 4.6.
  2. Raw 4D functional (task) image, .nii or .nii.gz, for your site's emotion-processing task (see your Site Confirmation Packet, "fMRI Task Contrast," for the task name and condition list).
  3. Field map images, if available (Siemens phase/magnitude pairs, Philips field-map + magnitude, or blip-up/blip-down AP/PA pairs), with their acquisition metadata (echo spacing, echo times, etc.).
  4. Event files with the onset and duration of every condition of your task, in SPM MAT, FSL 3-column, or BIDS TSV format. The contrast of interest in this project is the negative emotion condition versus the neutral condition (detailed in Section 1.4), so the event file must include a negative emotion condition. For sites with multiple types of negative emotion (e.g., fear, anger, and sadness), aggregate these into a single negative emotion condition in the event file.

    Example of a BIDS TSV events file (onsets are in seconds).

  5. A group-level covariate spreadsheet (CSV, TSV, or XLSX) with one row per subject and the following columns:
    • ID — identical to the subject IDs used in your image file names.
    • Age (in years).
    • Biological sex, coded "M" and "F".
    • Your site's harmonized parenting construct score(s), using the exact subscale(s) confirmed in your Site Confirmation Packet (e.g., PBI-Care for Warmth/Responsiveness, APQ-Inconsistent Discipline, MAPS Physical Control for Harsh/Reactive Control, etc.). Only include the constructs your site contributes.
    • Any optional secondary-analysis covariates your site is using (race/ethnicity, parental education, SES, etc. — see your study proposal and the "Secondary analysis" row of your Site Confirmation Packet model table).

1.3 If Your Task Has a Performance-Dependent Component

If your task has a correct/incorrect or reaction-time-dependent aspect, calculate a per-participant accuracy score (0–1, mean across trials) and exclude participants whose score falls more than 2 SD below the sample mean by removing their row from the covariate spreadsheet. This automatically excludes them from the group analysis.

1.4 Defining Your Task Contrast

Every site in the Parenting IBMA project contrasts a negative emotional condition against a neutral/control condition, but the specific conditions differ by task. Using your Site Confirmation Packet's "fMRI Task Contrast" row for your site as a reference:

  1. Note the exact condition names in your event files that make up the "negative emotional" side of the contrast (e.g., angry/fearful/sad faces, negative images, "observe affect," etc.) and the condition(s) that make up the neutral/control side (e.g., neutral faces, shapes, rest/baseline).
  2. Assign +1 to each condition on the negative emotional side and −1 to each condition on the neutral/control side, and 0 to any other modeled condition not part of this contrast.
  3. Important: we also examine the reversed contrast, which assigns +1 to the neutral/control condition and −1 to the negative emotional condition, and 0 to any other modeled condition not part of this contrast. Make sure the contrast is specified using +1, −1, and 0 weights, with the maximum contrast weight (peak) set to 1.0 and the sum of all condition weights equal to 0.
  4. This is why a general negative emotion condition must be defined in the event file. Do not use contrasts such as [1, 1, −2, 0], where different negative emotion conditions are assigned separate weights. Instead, aggregate the different negative emotion conditions (e.g., fear, anger, and sadness) into a single negative emotion condition so the contrast can be consistently specified as [1, −1, 0, …].
Unsure how to set up your contrast vector? Contact junxuan@student.unimelb.edu.au before running HALFpipe. An incorrectly specified contrast cannot be pooled with the rest of the sample.

1.5 Calculating Your High-Pass Filter Width

For each task condition, calculate the time difference in seconds between the onset of one event/block and the next onset of that same condition. Take the maximum difference across all conditions and all subjects, and multiply by 1.5. If the result is smaller than 125 s, use 125 s as your high-pass filter width; otherwise use the calculated value.

Example: a block design with a 30 s experimental block alternating with a 30 s control block has a 60 s onset-to-onset interval. 60 × 1.5 = 90 s, which is below 125 s, so the filter width is 125 s. If some conditions are performance-dependent (and so vary in timing across subjects), use the maximum value observed anywhere in your sample.

Step 2. Install a Container Platform

This step is only needed once per machine.

  1. Open a terminal (on Windows, use Docker Desktop's terminal).
  2. Type apptainer or singularity and press enter. If you get usage instructions rather than command not found, you already have a container platform — skip to Step 3.
  3. Only if running on an HPC Cluster: try module load singularity (or apptainer) to load it as an optional module. You will need to re-run this every time you log back in or start a new node.
  4. Choose a platform for your system:
Container platform options
PlatformWhere to use itHow to install
Docker DesktopMac / Windows Local MachineInstall from docker.com/products/docker-desktop
ApptainerLinux workstation or HPC (preferred on newer systems) Local Machine HPC Clustersudo apt install -y apptainer, or see the sylabs.io install guide
Singularity 3.xLinux workstation or HPC Local Machine HPC ClusterFollow the Singularity 3.x Quick Start guide
Singularity 2.xOlder HPC clusters HPC Clustersudo apt install singularity-container

After installing (or loading the module), re-run the command from Step 2 to confirm it works.

Step 3. Download HALFpipe & Set Up Working Directory

The Parenting IBMA project uses HALFpipe v1.3.2. Even if you already have HALFpipe installed or have previously used it for processing, please re-download the recommended release.

Download commands by platform
PlatformCommand
Apptainer / Singularity 3.xcurl -O https://download.fmri.science/singularity/halfpipe-1.3.2.sif
Singularity 2.xcurl -O https://download.fmri.science/singularity/halfpipe-1.3.2.simg
Docker Desktopdocker pull --platform linux/amd64 halfpipe/halfpipe:1.3.2
  • If using Apptainer/Singularity: run find $(pwd) -maxdepth 1 to confirm the halfpipe-1.3.2.sif/.simg file downloaded, and note its full path. You'll need it in Step 4.
  • If using Docker: no file path is needed — Docker stores the image internally.

3.1 Set Up Your Working Directory

  1. Create an empty base directory with enough free disk space (see Section 1.1), e.g. mkdir parenting_ibma && cd parenting_ibma.
  2. Create a working directory inside it for HALFpipe's outputs, e.g. mkdir working_dir.
  3. Place a copy of your FreeSurfer license file (license.txt) inside the working directory, or point to it later with the --fs-license-file flag.
Run HALFpipe once per cohort/site. If your site has more than one scanner or sub-cohort with materially different acquisition parameters (e.g., different TRs), use a separate working directory for each.

Step 4. Run Preprocessing and Feature Extraction

4.1 Launching HALFpipe

Local Machine Running HALFpipe on a local computer
  1. Open a terminal session (if using Docker, open the terminal via Docker Desktop).
  2. Run the appropriate command for your container platform below.
Launch commands — local machine
ContextCommand
Singularity or Apptainer (3.x)singularity run --contain --cleanenv --bind /:/ext \
halfpipe-1.3.2.sif --subject-chunks --nipype-n-procs 1 --keep none
Singularity (2.x)singularity run --contain --cleanenv --bind /:/ext \
halfpipe-1.3.2.simg --subject-chunks --nipype-n-procs 1 --keep none
Docker Desktop — macOSdocker run --interactive --tty --volume /:/ext \
halfpipe/halfpipe:1.3.2 --subject-chunks --nipype-n-procs 1 --keep none
Docker Desktop — Windowsdocker run --interactive --tty --volume C:/:/ext \
halfpipe/halfpipe:1.3.2 --subject-chunks --nipype-n-procs 1 --keep none
Use forward slashes (/) instead of backslashes in file paths, and replace C: with the appropriate drive letter for your system.

Replace halfpipe-1.3.2.sif with the actual path to the file you downloaded. --subject-chunks and --nipype-n-procs 1 are optional throttling flags — they slow things down but help avoid overloading a laptop or workstation.

HPC Cluster Running HALFpipe on an HPC
  1. Open a terminal session and connect to your HPC.
  2. Start an interactive job on the cluster to run the HALFpipe container. Refer to your HPC's documentation or IT support for the exact syntax; a few common examples are given below.
Starting an interactive job by job manager
Job managerCommand
SLURMsrun --time 0-6 --ntasks=1 --pty bash
SGEqlogin -now no
Torque / PBSqsub -I -l walltime=12:00:00

Then load the Singularity/Apptainer package: module load singularity or module load apptainer.

Once an interactive session is allocated to you, start the pipeline as follows:

Launch commands — HPC (after allocation)
ContextCommand
Singularity (3.x)singularity run --contain --cleanenv --bind /:/ext halfpipe-1.3.2.sif --use-cluster
Singularity (2.x)singularity run --contain --cleanenv --bind /:/ext halfpipe-1.3.2.simg --use-cluster
Apptainerapptainer run --contain --cleanenv --bind /:/ext halfpipe-1.3.2.sif --use-cluster

File location: ensure the halfpipe-1.3.2.sif file is in your current working directory, or specify its full path.
Directory binding: the --bind (or -B) option maps directories from your host system into the container — for example, /home/user/Documents on the host becomes /ext/home/user/Documents inside the container.
Cluster flag: use --use-cluster when running the execution command on an HPC.

4.2 Pipeline Settings

You have now opened the user interface, which should look like this:

You can use Ctrl-C at any point to go back a step.

  1. Specify the working directory — the folder created in Section 3.1.
  2. Is the data available in BIDS format?
    • Yes → enter the path to your BIDS directory and continue to Step 6 below.
    • No → continue with the sub-steps below.
  3. Specify the path of the T1-weighted image files, using the {subject} tag in place of the subject ID (e.g. /path/to/T1/{subject}/T1.nii.gz). HALFpipe will report how many files/subjects it found — for example: "Found 31 files for 31 subjects."
  4. Specify the path of the BOLD image files the same way, using {subject} (and {task} if you have more than one task).
  5. If no task name was specified, specify the task name (e.g. affect_labelling).
  6. Check that the repetition time (TR) shown is correct for your data. A TR of 1 s is sometimes mis-set in headers created by concatenating 3D volumes — correct this manually if so.
  7. Add more BOLD image files? Say Yes if you need to add data with a different folder structure or metadata (e.g. a different TR), otherwise No.
  8. Do slice timing? Yes if you have the acquisition's slice-timing details (check with your MR physicist/technician if unsure); confirm or correct the detected slice order and timing values. Otherwise No.
  9. Remove initial volumes from scans? Enter 0 unless your data needs equilibration volumes discarded.
  10. Specify field maps? Yes if you acquired them (you'll be asked for their type, file names, and acquisition parameters) — this step is skipped automatically for BIDS input. Otherwise No.

4.3 First-Level (Task) Feature — Three Confound-Regression Variations

Specify first-level features? Select Yes.

Write down the name of your site's task (see your Site Confirmation Packet). For each task, loop through the feature-specification steps below three times, changing only the confound-regression setting each time, so that downstream analyses can confirm results are not an artifact of the confound strategy. Give each repetition a distinct feature name, e.g. facesVar1, facesVar2, facesVar3.

4.4 Group-Level Model(s)

Your Site Confirmation Packet lists up to three model families per parenting construct you contribute: Primary models, Moderation models, and Secondary models. Set up one HALFpipe group-level model per row you intend to run. For each:

Group-level model specification
PromptWhat to enter
Specify group-level model?Yes
Specify model typeLinear model
Specify model nameSomething identifiable, e.g. warmth_primary, harsh_moderation
Aggregate scan-level statistics before analysis? (multi-run tasks only)Select the run/acquisition/session tags marked with a star [*]
Specify features to useSelect all features marked with a star [*]
Specify the path of the covariates/group data spreadsheet filePath to the spreadsheet from Section 1.2, item 5
Specify the column containing subject namesYour ID column
Specify the column data typesSet each column's type correctly (numeric for Age/construct scores, categorical for Sex)
Subjects to useAll (star [*]). Deselect only if you're intentionally excluding a sub-group
Exclude subjects based on movement?Yes, confirm the default settings
Specify the maximum allowed mean framewise displacement (mm)0.5

Specify the action for missing valuesListwise deletion for all (default)
Specify additional contrasts for categorical variables?No

Secondary-analysis models add optional covariates (race/ethnicity, parental education, SES, etc.) on top of the Primary model. See your study proposal and the "Secondary analysis" row of your Site Confirmation Packet for exactly which covariates apply to your site.

HALFpipe will now begin processing. This may take some time.

4.5 If Running on an HPC

HPC Cluster

HALFpipe will now generate and validate the commands to run for preprocessing and analysis. This can take up to a few hours if you have dozens of subjects.

Once the program terminates, check your working directory for the following files and folders: derivatives, nipype, rawdata, reports, work, workflow***.pickle.xz, execgraph***.pickle.xz, and one of submit.slurm.sh, submit.pbs.sh, or submit.sge.sh.

Open the automatically generated submit file and compare it to the example provided below:

  1. Make sure the path associated with the --bind flag is the same one you used to launch the pipeline.
  2. Verify that all paths are correct.
  3. If necessary, edit the script (e.g. add #SBATCH --account=def-account to submit.slurm.sh). If you are unsure, refer to your HPC's documentation or contact your IT support.

Depending on your cluster's configuration (e.g., SGE or Torque), these modifications may need to be applied to a different submit file than the SLURM example shown here. Please consult your cluster's documentation or contact your IT support team to confirm.

Example submit.slurm.sh file generated by HALFpipe:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=halfpipe
#SBATCH --output=halfpipe.log.txt
#SBATCH --time=1-0
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=2
#SBATCH --mem=25258M
#SBATCH --array=1-37

if ! [ -x "$(command -v singularity)" ]; then
    module load singularity
fi

singularity run \
  --contain --cleanenv \
  --bind /:/ext \
  /home/username/projects/containers/halfpipe-1.3.2.sif \
  --workdir /ext/home/username/projects/working_directory \
  --only-run \
  --uuid 5cbac59b \
  --subject-list /ext/home/username/projects/working_directory/subject-list.txt \
  --subject-chunks \
  --only-chunk-index ${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID} \
  --nipype-n-procs 2 \
  --keep some

Finally, submit the script to the HPC queue:

Submitting the preprocessing job by job manager
Job managerCommand
SLURMsbatch submit.slurm.sh
SGEqsub submit.sge.sh
Torque/PBSqsub submit.torque.sh
HALFpipe will now begin processing. This may take some time.

Local Machine If you are running HALFpipe on a local computer, the pipeline will have already started at this point — there is no separate submission step.

4.6 If Your Only Anatomical Images Are Already Skull-Stripped

Press Ctrl-C to stop the program before it finishes generating commands. Open spec.json in the working directory in a text editor, find "skull_strip_algorithm": "ants", change "ants" to "none", and save. Restart HALFpipe, select the same working directory, and choose "Run without modification" when it detects the existing spec file.

4.7 Check Pre-Processing and Re-Run If Necessary

Open a terminal, navigate to your working directory, and run:

for i in $(strings graphs.*.dat | grep features_wf | grep result_make_resultdicts_b.pklz | sed 's|^/ext||g'); do
  if [ ! -f ${i} ]; then
    echo ${i} | sed "s/^.*single_subject_\([A-Za-z0-9]*\)_wf.*$/\1/p";
  fi;
done | sort | uniq | tee subject-list.txt

This prints any subjects that did not finish processing and writes their IDs to subject-list.txt in the working directory (you can also hand-edit this file, e.g. to add newly arrived participants).

  • Local Machine Re-run HALFpipe with the same command as before, adding --subject-list <full path to subject-list.txt> at the end, then select "Run without modification."
  • HPC Cluster Add the same option to your submission script and resubmit.
  • You can also use --subject-include <characters> to (re-)run only subjects whose ID contains those characters.

Step 5. Quality Assessment

  • HPC Cluster If you ran on an HPC, copy the reports folder from your working directory to a machine where you can comfortably review it.

Complete the QC ratings using the HALFpipe quality-control guide.

Note: the quality-control guide was developed for resting-state data. In its example report, "task" refers to resting state, whereas in our case it refers to the emotion-processing task.

Contact the coordinating site if you're unsure about a particular image and can't resolve it with a local scanner technician or MR physicist.

Step 6. Submit Group-Level Analysis

Once preprocessing and first-level modeling have completed and passed QC, you can start running group-level analysis. Although the group-level model was already specified in Step 4.4, HALFpipe only completes first-level analysis by default, so a separate job must be submitted to run the group-level analysis.

HPC Cluster

In the working directory (make sure a derivatives folder was generated from the previous step), create a submit-model job file (for example, submit-model.slurm):

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=halfpipe-model
#SBATCH --output=/path/to/the/working/directory/model-%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/path/to/the/working/directory/model-%j.err
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=64G

module load foss/2022a
module load Apptainer/1.1.8   # adjust based on your own HPC setting

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
export NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1

singularity run \
  --containall \
  --bind /:/ext \
  --bind /tmp:/tmp \
  /path/to/halfpipe-1.3.2.sif \
  --nipype-n-procs 4 \
  --nipype-omp-nthreads 1 \
  --nipype-memory-gb 60 \
  --verbose \
  group-level \
  --from-spec \
  --workdir /path/to/the/working/directory

Depending on your cluster's configuration (e.g., SGE or Torque), these modifications may need to be applied to a different submit file than the SLURM example shown here. Please consult your cluster's documentation or contact your IT support team to confirm.

Then submit the submit-model job file:

Submitting the group-level job by job manager
Job managerCommand
SLURMsbatch submit-model.slurm
SGEqsub submit-model.sge
Torque/PBSqsub submit-model.torque
Local Machine

You do not need to submit an interactive job. An example group-level analysis command is below:

singularity run \
  --containall \
  --bind /:/ext \
  --bind /tmp:/tmp \
  /path/to/halfpipe-1.3.2.sif \
  --nipype-n-procs 4 \
  --nipype-omp-nthreads 1 \
  --nipype-memory-gb 12 \
  --verbose \
  group-level \
  --from-spec \
  --workdir /path/to/the/working/directory \
  > >(tee /path/to/the/working/directory/model.out) \
  2> >(tee /path/to/the/working/directory/model.err >&2)

If you have any questions regarding the group-level job file, please feel free to contact us — we'll be happy to help troubleshoot any issue.

HALFpipe will now begin processing the group-level model. This may take some time.

Step 7. Upload Results for the IBMA Deadline: 31 December 2026

7.1 Download Data Mover

Each site has a shareable link for uploading group-level files to the project leadership team. You will use Data Mover when you receive a shareable link in the Site Confirmation Packet PDF file. When you click the link, the Data Mover client starts automatically if it is already installed; otherwise, your web browser will download the installer.

Once started, Data Mover presents a simple GUI for uploading data. Click Add new and paste the shareable link to proceed. If you are using Windows or macOS, you can skip the manual Data Mover download steps below.

Currently, Linux installation must be done manually:

Preparation

  1. When doing a new install, remove any .jar files you may have downloaded (part of the auto-update process; see the Check step below) from your .Arcitecta/DataMover/updates folder (under your home directory). If you don't remove these, they will conflict with the newly installed version.
  2. Uninstall the old version of the app (or simply install over the top of it). Do not rename the old application, as this may cause conflicts — if you want to keep an earlier version, zip up the old application first.

Download

  1. Visit mediaflux.researchsoftware.unimelb.edu.au/mflux/data/mover and download the version for your operating system (macOS, Windows 10, or Linux).
  2. To download a specific version with a tool such as curl or wget, use:
    • macOS: Mediaflux Data Mover.dmg
    • Windows: Mediaflux Data Mover.msi
    • Linux: mediaflux-data-mover.zip

Install (Linux)

  1. Unpack the mediaflux-data-mover.zip file. The resulting mediaflux-data-mover directory must not be stored in a path that contains bin as one of its elements, due to a Linux Java bug (avoid /usr/local/bin or ~/bin, for example).
  2. Make the binary executable: chmod +x mediaflux-data-mover/bin/mediaflux-data-mover.
  3. Optionally, add <path>/mediaflux-data-mover/bin to your PATH variable.
  4. Optionally, read the README.txt for instructions on configuring your web browser to automatically open arcio links with Data Mover.

Check

After installing, start Data Mover and confirm the version shown (bottom left of the GUI) is the version you expect.

7.2 Uploading Results

Each site has its own Mediaflux folder, and other sites cannot access the files in that folder. Once preprocessing, first-level modeling, and your group-level model(s) from Step 6 have completed and passed QC:

  1. Locate the group-level summary statistic (contrast) maps in the grouplevel/ folder of your working directory — one set per model you specified. Package the summary maps (the whole grouplevel folder) together with the model spec (spec.json and reportvals.txt) and a brief note on which subscale(s) you used for each construct (per your confirmed Site Confirmation Packet mapping).
  2. Complete the Parenting-IBMA results upload.xlsx file. This asks for additional information about the fMRI scan settings, demographic characteristics, and authorship for the meta-analysis paper. Each site can nominate co-authors based on their contributions to this project.
  3. Send the files to the coordinating site using a password-protected shareable link, following the data-transfer method specified by the coordinating team.
